recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If specific OrderingService guidance is still desired, a proponent or work group should open a fresh issue with concrete proposed text and references rather than inferring a source edit from FHIR-14776 alone.
issue_request: FHIR-14776 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 ballot change request for the FHIR-core workflow section asking FHIR-I to consider SOA OrderingService work and the related OMG technical submission as input to workflow section 12.7.5.
initial_application: No Jira-tagged source commit for FHIR-14776 was found. The active workflow pages already include service-based workflow coverage: source/workflow.html names Services as a workflow execution paradigm, and source/workflow-ad-hoc.html includes Option E for service requests from placer to filler, introduced before FHIR-14776.
additional_context: January 2018 WGM minutes recorded FHIR-14776 as Persuasive. Workflow minutes in 2022 grouped FHIR-14776 with adjacent OMG alignment issue FHIR-14770 for possible reopening/rejection, and FHIR-I minutes on 2023-03-20 recorded that there was not enough quorum to reopen FHIR-14776, FHIR-I had done the investigation, and the ticket was closed. Searches found no substantive Zulip discussion or concrete SOA OrderingService wording to apply.
reconciliation: No source change was made. A source edit now would require inventing OrderingService or OMG wording that the final Jira and meeting records do not specify, while the current active workflow pages already acknowledge service-based workflow as an experience-limited pattern.

related_jiras.note: Adjacent Published workflow issue about OMG Healthcare Business Process alignment was discussed with FHIR-14776 and already has a separate no-change audit commit on the combined branch.
